chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ṣafwān, who said:

A man asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام while I was present, and he said: “I have a wound in my anus. I perform wudu (ablution), then do istinjāʾ, then after that I find moisture and yellowness coming out from the anus, so I repeat the wudu (ablution).”
He said: “Have you cleansed it thoroughly?” He said: “Yes.”
He said: “No; rather, sprinkle it with water, and do not repeat the wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.أَسْتَنْجِي: I cleanse the private area after relieving oneself
key_terms.الصُّفْرَةَ: yellowish discharge निकलting from the wound area
key_terms.جُرْحًا: a wound affecting the legal ruling discussed
key_terms.مَقْعَدَتِي: my anus; the bodily location mentioned in the question

ai.seo_question: Does discharge from a wound near the anus require repeating wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning discharge from a wound near the anus after cleaning. Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام instructs that after proper cleansing, one should only sprinkle the area with water and not repeat wudu (ablution), indicating that such moisture does not nullify ritual purity in this case.
